sources.citation: Janzen, Correna & Elvira Corbalan. 2019. Sos Kundi - English - Tok Pisin Dictionary. SIL PNG / Webonary.
sources.note: Sister language split from the same ISO code (68% lexical similarity); a Webonary dictionary front matter often carries a phonology/orthography note including stress, which would at least characterise the closest documented variety (not Keak itself).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record keak1239 (JSON + page) and Glottolog 5.1 CLDF sources.bib entries tagged [keh]
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog's most extensive description = Laycock 1968 'a wordlist or less'; zero descriptive refs. The six [keh]-tagged entries are Aitken 1990 (drum signals), Laycock 1968, Laycock 1973, ISO CR 2008-022, Richardson & Tupper 2013 (socling), Schindlbeck 1980 (ethnography). Page lists subclassification comments Staalsen 1975: 11, Richardson & Tupper 2013, Jendraschek 2012: 4-8.

sources.citation: Richardson, Dan & Ian Tupper. 2013. Drawing language boundaries and assigning names: the cases of Sos Kundi and Ambakich. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-005. 21 pp.
sources.note: The only publication whose language tags include Keak [keh]; a sociolinguistic survey (2005 fieldwork) that may carry wordlists with stress marks or a phonological remark, and fixes the Keak/Sos Kundi identity. Glottolog holds a private PDF (papua\).

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 2008. The Manambu language of East Sepik, Papua New Guinea. Oxford: OUP. Ch.1, note 3.
sources.note: Nothing on Keak stress; identity only: 'of these [Sawos varieties], Sengo, Burui, Kwaruwi Kundi, and also Gaikundi appear to be members of the Iatmul continuum.. A reliable reappraisal of the languages covered by Sawos is in Staalsen (1975).'

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority [requester Dan Richardson, SIL PNG]. 2008. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Keak [keh] (associated change request 2008-022), dated 2008-04-11. 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Its value is negative evidence from the SIL surveyor himself: literature 'no newspapers, radion or television broadcasts. Maybe some scripture portions'; sources 'Sociolinguistic survey, 2005' and 'Some personal communication with a local translator'; the field 'Knowledge from published sources. Include known dictionaries, grammars, etc.' is left blank.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2008. Change Request 2008-022: split [sic] Malinguat into Keak [keh] and Sos Kundi [sdk] (adopted 2009-01-16). Submitted by Dan Richardson (SIL PNG), 2007-12-14. 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Administrative form only: 'The two languages are not inherently intelligible.. the lexical similarity of the two languages is 68%; there is no common literature' (p.3). Notes a forthcoming paper by Richardson on Sos Kundi and Ambakich (p.4).

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Iatmul (Sawos Dialect)' (glottocode iatm1242; source Foley 2005; 18 lexical items)
sources.note: Wordlist only, filed under Iatmul, no stress marks, no prose.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. & John A. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 731-766. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Ndu section: Abelam phoneme inventory /p t c k b d j g m n ny ng v r l w y a A aa/ 'fairly representative of Ndu Family languages', prenasalised voiced stops, orthography suggestions, pronoun paradigms, verb morphology, sentence-medial verbs; Iatmul notes from Staalsen. No statement on stress, accent or tone for any Ndu language, and nothing on Sawos/Keak phonology. Text searched in full for stress/accent/tone/pitch (0 relevant hits).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entry 91 SAWOS (Gaikunti, Kwongai, Sepik Plains, Tshuosh, Tshwosh), pp.27-28.
sources.note: Nothing. Village list and dialect labels; 'Brief mention in Laycock (1965a; 1968:47).. No real dialect surveys have been undertaken, and there may be at least two distinct languages subsumed under Sawos' (p.27); names Schanely's unpublished phonemic statement of Gaikunti (p.28).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU. Ch.14 'Notes on the Sawos language', pp.143-144; sec.18.24.
sources.note: Nothing for Sawos/Keak: 14.13 'it was not possible to elicit material in Sawos. Only two speakers of the language were encountered, and these only briefly' (p.144). The only stress section (5.2, pp.29-30) is for Wosera Abelam. No phonology of Sawos at all.
No phonology; alt names Kwaruwikwundi, Mevembet; cites Ethnologue 16 and the Endangered Languages Project only.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Family-level overview of Ndu phonology; may generalise about stress in Ndu/Iatmulic varieties, though not Keak-specific.

sources.citation: Jendraschek, Gerd. 2012. A grammar of Iatmul. Habilitationsschrift, Universität Regensburg. xv+564 pp. (pp.4-8 on the Sawos/Iatmul-continuum varieties; stress pp.91-93)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: If Keak (Kwaruwi Kundi) is a member of the Iatmul continuum as Aikhenvald 2008 suggests, this is the modern grammar whose stress rule (long vowels > CVC > initial syllable, per the Iatmul check) would be the closest description; pp.4-8 discuss which Sawos varieties belong to Iatmul.

sources.citation: Staalsen, Philip. 1975. The languages of the Sawos region (New Guinea). Anthropos 70(1/2): 6-16.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The reappraisal of the 'Sawos' varieties (incl. Kwaruwi Kundi = Keak) that Aikhenvald 2008 and Glottolog rely on; a survey with wordlists that may include a brief phonological/stress note per variety.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1968. Languages of the Lumi Subdistrict (West Sepik District), New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 7(1): 36-66.
